description: The bar chart illustrates the average number of likes received by posts grouped by the angular similarity of their headlines, measured in degrees, with error bars indicating variability. The vertical axis, labeled “Avg. Likes,” ranges from 400 to 600 in increments of 50, while the horizontal axis, labeled “Most similar group of posts,” categorizes posts into five angular intervals: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450]. Each light blue bar represents the mean likes for its respective group, with the shortest bar corresponding to the (90,180] group at approximately 590 likes and the tallest bar corresponding to the (360,450] group at approximately 620 likes. Error bars extend above and below each bar, suggesting measurement uncertainty or standard deviation. The chart is tilted diagonally, and the bars are arranged in ascending order of angular range, with no explicit sorting by magnitude, though a general upward trend in average likes is visible from left to right. The visual design emphasizes the relationship between headline similarity (in angular space) and social media engagement, as studied in the paper “How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media.”
